children: MEXICO CITY--Inflation in Mexico gained pace in the first half of September amid increases in fresh food and energy costs, while core inflation eased from the second half of August.

The consumer price index rose 0.33% in the first two weeks of this month, pushing the 12-month rate up to 3.42% from 3.26% in the second half of August, national statistics institute Inegi said Thursday.
Core CPI, which excludes energy and perishable foods, rose 0.17% and was up 3.79% from a year earlier, down from 3.83% in the second half of August.

Fresh fruit and vegetable prices rose 3.38% in the first half of September, including a 23% increase in the price of tomatoes which have a heavy weighting in the index. Energy costs rose 0.33%. Services rose 0.21% with higher tuition fees at the start of the school year partially offset by a 0.07% decline in other services, which include restaurants, mobile phones and vacation packages.

The Bank of Mexico is expected to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 6.5% Thursday, staying on hold for a third consecutive time. The central bank expects inflation to reach its 3% target in the fourth quarter of 2027.
